b: – Weird and in person celebrations of books.
– Listening to a poem while doing my little stretches. The Library of Congress and Poetry Archive collections, to be specific.
– And I’m thankful in advance to the programmer who builds me a little widget or website that streams a random poem from these archives.
– The new Marlon James. I’m late to the party, but damn.
– Finding something cool in a pile of books someone is giving away.
– The major book awards no longer being afraid of support for Palestine, and Paradiso 17 and Huna winning NBAs.
– A really good pen. I’ve had two instances recently where I had a small bookstore coupon that I spent on luxe pens. Highly recommend treating yourself to a fine writing instrument.
– Funny novels with funny first person narrators.
– The tide continuing to turn against AI. I’m thankful we may see AI’s high water mark very soon.
– Getting to interview Adam Peterson for the release of his story collection.
– Booksellers, who are in the middle of their most hectic season. I’m thankful for everyone who treats them reasonably this time of year.
– Peanuts, a Perfect Snack For Reading.
– Librarians, who are always in the middle of hectic season.
– Flaming Hydra, and especially Luke O’Neil’s recent New England Week which I’m revisiting as I pack up to go to Boston for the holiday.

– Connecting with a stranger over a book, especially that thing where someone points at your book from a distance, and you close it and hold up the cover, and they give you a thumbs up. Really good stuff.
– Small presses, and all the cool and weird things they’re taking a chance on.
– Marilynne Robinson. Her middle name is Summers, but she’s an autumn writer.
– My sweet seven month old showing preferences for books. And I also chew on the books that I like, so I’m thankful that he inherited that trait from me.
– Trying to explain Gene Wolfe’s deal to someone for the first time.
– A small book you can read in an afternoon. Also having an afternoon free to read.
– Olga Ravn’s gift guide, which includes Ibuprofen and haunted dolls.
– Reading an author who is really going for it and trying something new. I appreciate someone taking a risk, regardless of the outcome. (Usually.)
– A friend asking for a book recommendation, and then actually reading your recommendation, and then telling you they liked your recommendation. No better feeling in the world.
